title: Finding Adjectives and Adverbs in Sentences

instruction.text: Match the definitions with the words they describe.

atoms.a: A describing word which tells you more about a person, an animal, a place or a thing.
A describing word which tells you how an action takes place.

wrong.text: Adjectives are describing words which tell you more about a person, an animal, a place or a thing.

atoms.sound: The old sea turtle swims slowly.

wrong.text: Adverbs are describing words which tell you how an action takes place.
Adjectives are describing words which tell you more about a person, an animal, a place or a thing.

atoms.b: Kevin’s brother sloppily irons his ((blue)) shirt.
atoms.sound: Kevin’s brother sloppily irons his blue shirt.

wrong.text: Adverbs are describing words which tell you how an action takes place.

atoms.b: Kevin’s brother ((sloppily)) irons his blue shirt.

wrong.text: Adjectives are describing words which tell you more about a person, an animal, a place or a thing.

atoms.b: The ((friendly)) waitress takes their orders patiently.
atoms.sound: The friendly waitress takes their orders patiently.

wrong.text: Adverbs are describing words which tell you how an action takes place.

atoms.b: The friendly waitress takes their orders ((patiently)).

instruction.text: Are the words abverbs or adjectives? Put the words into the right group.

wrong.text:

Adverbs are describing words which tell you how an action takes place.
